hypotheses.justification: The statement also holds when `SearchTree.Lt T Γ` is well-founded, so a proof can split on `WellFounded (SearchTree.Lt T Γ)`. If it is not well-founded, the current proof works unchanged. If it is well-founded, the argument depends on these definitions. `chainU T Γ = descendingChain (SearchTree.Lt T Γ) ⊤`, and `descendingChain r z (i+1) = @Classical.epsilon α ⟨z⟩ (fun y => y ≺ descendingChain r z i ∧ ¬Acc r y)` (Vorspiel/Order.lean). `Classical.epsilon p` is `(strongIndefiniteDescription p h).val`, and in Init/Classical.lean that is `dite (∃ x, p x) … (fun _ => ⟨choice h, _⟩)`. Under well-foundedness every element is `Acc`, so no predicate `y ≺ chainU i ∧ ¬Acc y` has a witness. The negative branch returns `Classical.choice ⟨⊤⟩`, which does not depend on the predicate. So `chainU i = c := Classical.choice ⟨⊤⟩` for every `i ≥ 1`. Given `s ≤ u`: if `s ≥ 1`, then `chain s = c.seq = chain u`, which is trivial. If `s = 0`, then `chain 0 = Γ` (via `seq_top`), and we need `Γ ⊆ c.seq`. This holds for every search tree: induct on `SearchTreeAux T Γ n Δ`. The `zero` case gives `Γ ⊆ Γ`. The `succ a r` case gives `Γ ⊆ Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂`, using `ReduxNat.antimonotone r`, which needs only the Encodable instances. Both cases prove the conclusion, so `nwf` can be deleted. The remaining Encodable instances cannot be removed, because `chain`/`SearchTree`/`ReduxNat` need them to elaborate.
